extracted.intended_audience: researchers and students of digital culture, memetics, multimodal communication, and political/humor studies
extracted.subtask_description: Frameworks and analytic criteria for studying, evaluating, or using internet memes (multimodal humor artifacts) across research, pedagogy, and platform analysis. Covers qualities of 'good' memes, pedagogical selection criteria, analytic dimensions, and markers of platform-specific memetic behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good memes — six qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Good memes have six qualities, including a focus on ordinary people, humor, simplicity, flawed masculinity, replicability, and whimsical content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A simple meme could be easily stored and recalled. (Context: presented as characteristics associated with successful/‘good’ memes in the literature.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for successful learning memes (pharmacology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Six themes emerged as criteria for a successful learning experience of meme use: previous scientific background on the meme topic; scenario context of the meme; learning concepts tackled by memes; the simplicity of meme's message; the relevance of meme's message to practice; and the modality of meme's use in the topic of education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These themes were derived from thematic content analysis of student and faculty perceptions; the authors conclude that careful selection of memes (meeting these criteria) is required to ensure a successful educational experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markers of participatory propaganda on TikTok
rubrics_metrics.description: Five key markers of participatory propaganda: remixability; calls to action; coordination between official and unofficial actors; aesthetic and affective prioritization; and snowball virality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dynamics were observed in TikTok campaign data and are said to unfold through TikTok edits, vibes, and audio memes; they indicate how platform-specific vernaculars reshape campaign communication and diffusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation criteria for MLLM explanations of figurative meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating multimodal LLMs on figurative meaning in memes, human evaluation should assess whether the provided reasoning supports the predicted label and whether it remains faithful to the original meme content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in benchmarking studies: also note models' bias (tendency to label memes as figurative) and that correct predictions do not always accompany faithful explanations; evaluation thus requires judging both label correctness and explanation faithfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presupposition types used in political memes
rubrics_metrics.description: Political memes employ presuppositions of several types: existential, lexical, structural, and counterfactual presuppositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These presuppositions encode implicit assumptions about political actors, institutions, and events, rely on shared background knowledge, and function as pragmatic strategies for embedding ideological critique or satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four dimensions for cross-cultural analysis of user-generated content
rubrics_metrics.description: To analyze cross-cultural UGC (including memes) use four dimensions: values, frames, emotions, and communicative stances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genres should be used as prisms through which these dimensions are evaluated; the framework helps identify global and local aspects of digital cultures and cautions that prior theories of values may not fully account for UGC's multifaceted ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagefare analytical framework for political satire
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical framework combining: goal with target; frame of reference with focus; and means with presentation for analyzing political cartoons and memes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The framework is implemented via multimodal discourse analysis to examine how satire functions in conflict contexts; it pairs specific analytic pairs (goal-target, frame-focus, means-presentation) to structure interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memetic properties / definition elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet memes are described as digital units with shared characteristics in content, form, or stance; they circulate by imitation and remixing and are popular combinations of images and text shared by users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inclusive memetic approach emphasizes imitation, replication, and participatory redistribution as core properties that enable the generation of derivatives and shared cultural experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relational properties of online content: cocreation and co-ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Online content (including memes) should be conceptualized by relational properties such as cocreation and co-ownership potentials; these relational dimensions influence online participation and content stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A game-theoretic perspective (stag hunt) is suggested: coordination can be improved by informing individuals about others' risk tolerance and sharing common knowledge; memes are characterized as publicly visible, easy to create, and often unconcerned with aesthetics—attributes that affect cocreation dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicative differences between memes and GIFs
rubrics_metrics.description: Memes often employ humor and sarcasm as dominant themes, whereas GIFs focus more on conveying happiness and inspiration-related emotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The distinction matters for content analysis: authors advocate examining memes and GIFs separately because of their distinctive content and communicative approaches and differing impacts on public perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of absurdity in memetic communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Absurd memes function as an adaptive strategy: deliberate suspension or destabilization of meaning (absurdity) can re-enable communication under interpretive strain and serve as a coping mechanism in ideologically saturated spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a formal principle ('Law of Absurdity as Mercy'): absurdity/irony/humor may be strategically used to preserve operability of interpretive systems rather than indicating epistemic failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image-macro structural elements: verbal and non-verbal integration
rubrics_metrics.description: The verbal and non-verbal components of image macros are not arbitrary; they reflect conceptual integration processes and are adapted to intertextual existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis should attend to how image (visual) templates provide contextual frameworks that shape interpretation of associated text, and how transformations (snowcloning, remixes) affect multimodality and a meme's lifecycle.
